articles.title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
articles.authors: Sinclair RCF, Beveridge G, Duckworth AD, Giddings A, Cholbi S, Guy GV, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years or older undergoing hip fracture surgery with anaemia
articles.outcomes: Primary: death or major adverse cardiac events including myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery. Secondary: all-cause mortality, quality of life at 120 days, cost-effectiveness and health economic outcomes
articles.take_home: This trial is testing whether giving blood transfusions to maintain higher haemoglobin levels during hip fracture surgery reduces heart problems and death compared with lower transfusion targets. Results are expected by late 2026.

articles.title: Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pyrhonen HS, Tham J, Stefansdottir A, Persson A, Malmgren L, Rogmark C
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged 65 years and over who had surgery
articles.sample_size: 166 patients analysed from 550 admitted (median age 85 years, 68% women)
articles.outcomes: Detection of infection within 30 days and 7 days after hip fracture surgery using plasma calprotectin compared with procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, and white blood cell count
articles.take_home: Plasma calprotectin was better at detecting infections after hip fracture surgery than procalcitonin and C-reactive protein, especially for infections occurring within 7 days, though its overall accuracy was moderate. White blood cell count performed similarly to calprotectin.

articles.title: Alcohol use is common in older patients with fall-related fractures: a secondary analysis from a prospective cohort study using PEth as an objective assessment of consumption.
articles.authors: Rogmark C, Malmgren L, Holmgren A, Magnusson A, Pyrhonen HS
articles.population: Older people aged 65 years and over admitted to hospital after a fall-related fracture
articles.outcomes: Alcohol consumption measured by phosphatidylethanol biomarker, frailty status, hyponatraemia, and 90-day mortality
articles.take_home: At least one in five older patients admitted with fall-related fractures had continuous alcohol consumption. Patients with higher alcohol consumption had increased risk of hyponatraemia but no other clear short-term negative effects were identified.

articles.title: Projected Lifetime Salary Compensation Between Academic and Non-Academic Careers in Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery.
articles.authors: Silvestre J, Minerva AJ, Jacques BA, Reid KR, Hartsock LA, Weaver MJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Financial analysis using net present value and Monte Carlo simulation
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma surgeons in academic and non-academic practice settings
articles.outcomes: Lifetime salary compensation comparison between academic and non-academic practices; compensation per work relative value unit; years required to reach salary parity
articles.take_home: Academic orthopaedic trauma surgeons earn significantly less over their lifetime than non-academic surgeons, earning 6.6% to 23.7% less depending on salary level, and would need 4 to 24 additional years of work to earn the same total amount. This lower pay is due to being paid less per unit of work done, not because academic surgeons do less work.

articles.title: Trends in Orthopaedic Trauma Research: A 30-Year Analysis of Orthopaedic Trauma Association Annual Meeting Abstracts, 1996-2025.
articles.authors: Rechter GR, Hedbany DT, Langford JR, Casin A, Haidukewych GJ, Shaath MK
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma research abstracts presented at the Orthopaedic Trauma Association Annual Meeting
articles.outcomes: Proportional changes in research topics across three decades, including anatomic regions studied and research themes
articles.take_home: Research into hip and proximal femur fractures has become increasingly common over the past 30 years and is now the most studied bone injury area, whilst research into spine, foot and children's injuries has declined. The amount of high-quality randomised controlled trial research has stayed roughly the same.

articles.title: Penetrating renal trauma in a high-complexity Latin American centre: Management patterns and renal preservation, 2013-2025 - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Londono Barrientos M, Arroyo P, Bernal C, Bran JD, Gallego DAG, Toro DAM, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with renal trauma (penetrating or blunt injury)
articles.outcomes: Nephrectomy rates, renal preservation with non-operative management and angioembolisation, in-hospital complications, management approach changes over 13 years
articles.take_home: Kidney-preserving treatments like watching carefully without surgery and angioembolisation (a minimally invasive procedure) successfully saved every kidney they were used for, including in penetrating injuries like gunshot wounds. Loss of kidney function was more related to the decision to perform open surgery than to the type of injury itself.

articles.title: A Prospective Randomized Trial to Assess Early versus Delayed Weight Bearing Following Operatively Treated Ankle Fractures in the United States.
articles.authors: Obremskey WT, Archer KR, Gaski GE, Gitajn IL, Natoli RM, Spitler CA, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with ankle fractures treated with surgery at 19 US trauma centres
articles.sample_size: 418 patients (214 early weight bearing, 204 delayed weight bearing)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation for complications (hardware failure, non-union, loss of reduction, infection or fusion) and time to return-to-work within 365 days
articles.take_home: Early weight bearing at 2 weeks after ankle fracture surgery was as safe as delayed weight bearing at 6 weeks, with similar rates of complications. However, early weight bearing did not significantly speed up return-to-work, with the early group returning to work around 15 days sooner on average.

articles.title: Incidence of severe mountain bike-related injuries and mortality: A 15-year statewide analysis.
articles.authors: Course G, Sharman JE, Otahal P, Tran V
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of hospital admission records
articles.population: Mountain bike riders in Tasmania, Australia admitted to hospital with severe injuries
articles.sample_size: 85 severe injuries from 6643 mountain bike-related emergency department presentations over 15 years
articles.outcomes: Incidence of severe mountain bike injuries requiring intensive care, neurosurgery high dependency unit admission, emergency surgery within 4 hours, or inter-state transfer. Secondary outcomes included injury mechanisms, body regions affected, and injury types.
articles.take_home: Severe mountain bike injuries increased over 15 years, with jump execution being the most common cause of serious injury. Most severe injuries affected the abdomen, neck and chest, and whilst severe injuries remained only 1.3% of all mountain bike emergency presentations, the rise in cases suggests the need for better trail design and injury prevention strategies.

articles.title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.
articles.authors: Sarmiento-Falen J, Arif HA, Szatkowski JP
articles.study_type: Narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies
articles.population: Patients with pilon fractures, particularly those with small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments
articles.outcomes: Maintained reduction, prevention of articular fragment displacement, improved support of the articular margin
articles.take_home: Rim plating may help control small anterior or anterolateral fragments in certain pilon fractures that standard plates cannot reliably support, particularly when the fragment is less than 15 mm tall. This technique acts as a peripheral buttress to prevent these shear-prone fragments from slipping out of position.

articles.title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
articles.authors: AlSumadi M, Chapman J, Akbar Z, Saragazi N, Newton A, Brown DJ
articles.population: Patients with distal radius fractures treated with volar locking plate
articles.sample_size: 92 patients (23 cases of fixation failure, 69 controls)
articles.outcomes: Association between radiological parameters and failure of fixation (post-operative fracture collapse or screw penetration)
articles.take_home: The study found that how well the fracture is reduced during surgery, particularly the gap between fracture fragments and their alignment, matters more for preventing fixation failure than the severity of the initial injury. However, radiological measurements alone do not reliably predict which patients will experience fixation failure.

articles.title: Association of neighborhood social vulnerability with reoperation after operative treatment of proximal humerus fractures.
articles.authors: Cohen EM, Kucharik MP, Bostrom N, Garcia JR, Bui A, Boughanem D, et al.
articles.population: Patients treated for acute proximal humerus fractures (broken upper arm bone near the shoulder)
articles.outcomes: Need for a second operation to fix complications after initial surgery
articles.take_home: Patients living in neighborhoods with higher social vulnerability scores were more likely to need a second operation after proximal humerus fracture surgery. The findings suggest neighborhood-level social factors may affect recovery outcomes, though further research is needed to confirm these results.

articles.title: Creation of a formal chest wall injury program improves compliance with rib fixation indications.
articles.authors: Muldiiarov V, Bouldoukian S, Khan H, Campbell A, Matos M, Kamien A, et al.
articles.population: Adults with radiographically confirmed rib fractures at a Level I trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 3488 patients, of whom 1629 met operative criteria for surgical stabilization
articles.outcomes: Proportion of eligible patients who received surgical rib fixation before and after implementation of a dedicated chest wall injury program
articles.take_home: Setting up a formal chest wall injury program with standardised guidelines and coordinated care significantly increased the rate of surgical rib fixation in eligible patients, rising from about 20% to 41%. This suggests that better organisation and communication between teams helps more patients who would benefit from surgery actually receive it.

articles.title: Postoperative morbidity among survivors of emergency war trauma surgery in a conflict setting: a descriptive cohort study.
articles.authors: Elbayoumi NE, Mezied G, Elbayoumi F, Alshawwa N, Shaikhkhalil H, Aladini M, et al.
articles.population: Civilians undergoing emergency surgery for conflict-related abdominal and thoracic trauma during the 2024 Gaza conflict
articles.sample_size: 79 patients (54 survivors analysed for postoperative complications)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative morbidity, infectious complications, surgical site infection, mortality, Injury Severity Score
articles.take_home: Most patients who survived to hospital discharge after emergency war trauma surgery developed complications, mainly infections including surgical site infections. Postoperative complications were common across all injury severity levels among survivors, whereas death was more closely linked to how severe the initial injury was.

articles.title: Surgeon preferences and educational gaps in the treatment of complex distal radius fractures in Latin America.
articles.authors: Arroyo Berezowsky C, Garcia Gomez A, Celeita Medina DC
articles.population: Orthopaedic and hand surgeons across Latin America
articles.outcomes: Treatment preferences for complex distal radius fractures based on surgeon age, fellowship training, and experience; factors influencing surgical decision-making
articles.take_home: Older surgeons preferred traditional treatment methods for complex wrist fractures, while those with hand surgery training were more likely to use advanced fixation techniques. Surgeon age and hand surgery training were the main factors affecting treatment choices.
